steps.text: Score flank steak by making shallow crisscross cuts on both sides.

Place olive oil, light brown sugar, red wine, soy sauce, onion powder, honey, green onions, garlic cloves, garlic vinegar, ground ginger, and garlic powder in a blender. Purée until smooth; pour mixture into a resealable plastic bag. Add steak, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours to overnight.
Remove steak from the refrigerator and pour marinade into a small saucepan. Allow steak to rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring marinade to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes; set aside.
Preheat an outdoor grill to medium-high heat, and lightly oil the grate.

Grill the steak on the preheated grill until it starts to firm up and is reddish-pink and juicy in the center, about 7 minutes per side, basting often with cooked marinade. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 130 degrees F (54 degrees C) for medium rare.

raw_recipe.headline: Flank Steak Marinade
raw_recipe.description: Light brown sugar and honey are blended with soy sauce, garlic, and green onion to make a savory sweet marinade for flank steak.

review.reviewBody: This was excellent. I have been buying marinated steak tips at The Meat House and this marinade is very close in taste to their's. I used red wine vinegar instead of garlic vinegar, and added a bit of kosher salt. I also used a little less brown sugar. It was FABULOUS.
Great flavorful marinade! Next time I will most likely slice this up before marinating to get the flavor all over the meat.

I used this recipe for skirt steak. It was THE BEST EVER!! We have a market in Santa Cruz that is awesome. This BEAT IT hands down.I had no honey, so I put 2 tbspns. of sugar instead. Either way, you cant miss with this!!
I slow roasted steak at 280 for 2 hours. I used the marinade to top steak when serving. It turned out medium and was very flavored.

This was a lot of ingredients! I didn't have flank steak so I used a 1" think slice of equally tough meat. I used a hand emulsion blender to grind it together. Just make sure that you do not cook the meat in the house as I did the first time. The meat will steam in the marinade and then burn in the pan becoming bitter tasting from the sugar in marinades. It makes clean-up a pain to. On the grill it worked fine, the next time, although I was hoping for a more juicy aftertaste. But, I guess when you start with a tough cut of meat marinades can only do so much. It did have a really nice smell on the grilll though, and the people I served it to seemed to like it.

I used this for my rib eyes. I did cut back on the oil and sugar by about half. Also don't have garlic vinegar so used a small squeeze if lemon for acidity. I loved the idea of blending the Marinade..i thought that was awesome . I've seen it done but never have done it myself...i think that right there makes all the difference. ..will use variations of this again.
Made this several times it’s delicious!! Substituted the garlic vinegar for balsamic vinegar! The sauce is to die for!!!
This was very good. Next time I will reduce the brown sugar by 1/2.
We liked this a lot. I substituted red wine with white wine, because I didn't have any, and omitted the ginger. I might use a little less sugar next time.
This was fabulous. My guests loved it. I followed the recipe almost exactly. I think I will use chopped shallots in place of the onion powder next time. Otherwise really great.

I used this on a sirloin tip steak and marinated about 5 hours. We thought it was pretty good, although not life-changing. The only difference I made was to use sunflower oil instead of olive oil (my son is allergic to olives) and to sub red wine vinegar and an extra garlic clove for the garlic vinegar, since I didn't have garlic vinegar.
Excellent and easy to make with plenty of flavor. I made adjustments to it as suggested by other users.
Made as directed. It was perfect. Will definitely make again-next time not grilling in a snow storm...lol
No changes and yes I will make it again!! It was a hit!! Great Job!!!
Tasty , easy . Definitely will make again.

This recipe is phenomenal! The only change I made? I didn't have garlic vinegar on hand so I used balsamic vinegar instead. I wondered about the intensity of so many similar spices in different forms but followed the recipe and the flank steak was "melt-in-your-mouth" - the flavours married perfectly! Thanks so much for sharing your family recipe Ron! Definite repeat!

This marinade is fantastic! I followed the recipe exactly. My guests all raved! Everyone loved it. My guests were gourmet cooks, so I was beyond happy they liked it. They ALL wanted the recipe! Just delicious!!!
It was a bit too sweet for our taste buds, next time I try this I will skip the brown sugar.

Made this today exactly like the recipe. It was ok. Very subtle flavors. Was hoping for a bit more. Still tasty, but I think I would try marinating it for at least 24hour plus next time. Only did about 6 hours this time.

This is an excellent recipe. Nice combination of flavors here. The next round, I think I'll leave out the brown sugar to experiment with making the marinade less sweet. I made this with a white wine and parm-regg risotto and it worked out really well. Overall, this is a winner!
